# A method on a unit or on a primitive that writes a top-level var compiles,
# and the write lands.
#
# Same lift as a struct method -- Go has no receiver for either, so both are
# free `LenDoubled(v Len, m *Model)` functions taking the Model as a trailing
# parameter -- but the three platform emit loops asked a narrower question than
# the call site did (structs and enums only), so the definition came out as
# `func (m *Model) doubled() Len` against a call to `LenDoubled`.

sngl test --platform=bubbletea --language=go app.sngl
stdout 'PASS'
! stdout 'FAIL'

-- app.sngl --
import . "sngl:test"
import . "sngl:ui"

unit Len {
    mm
    cm = 10mm
}

var log string = ""

func Len.doubled(v Len) Len {
    log = log + "!"
    return v + v
}

func int.twice(n int) int {
    log = log + "?"
    return n * 2
}

component main node {
    var five Len = 5mm
    var d Len = 0mm
    var t2 = 0
    var note = ""

    effect(@mount {
        d = five.doubled()
        t2 = 3.twice()
        note = log
    })

    text(value="{d}{t2}{note}")
}

func testUnitAndPrimitiveMethodsWriteTopLevelVar(t Test, c main) {
    t.assert(c.d == 10mm)
    t.assert(c.t2 == 6)
    t.assert(c.note == "!?")
}

window {
    main
}
